Unsigned 128-bit arithmetic helpers for add, sub, mul, shifts, msb, and division.

# Purpose
`fd_uwide.h` defines helper routines for unsigned 128-bit arithmetic on systems that do not provide native 128-bit integer support. It represents a 128-bit value as two `ulong` values, with the high word and low word stored as `<xh,xl>`, and it provides inline operations for addition, subtraction, increment, decrement, multiplication, bit shifts, and finding the most significant bit. These functions return carry, borrow, or inexact flags where needed, so callers can detect overflow, underflow, or lost bits.

The file also defines division support for 128-bit values by a 64-bit divisor. It includes private helper functions for division approximation and a general `fd_uwide_div` and `fd_uwide_divrem` implementation that compute the quotient, and for `fd_uwide_divrem` also the remainder. The code handles special cases such as zero divisors, power-of-two divisors, and small operands, then uses normalization and iterative correction for the general case. All functions are declared `static inline`, so this header is intended for direct inclusion by other C files that need these wide-integer operations.
